questions.question: Why is mobile LLM inference memory-bandwidth-bound rather than compute-bound?
options: Mobile chips lack dedicated matrix-multiplication units
Mobile DRAM bandwidth (50-90 GB/s) is 30-50x lower than datacenter HBM3 (2-3 TB/s), and decode is memory-bound
Mobile operating systems limit GPU compute time to extend battery life
Mobile models must run INT4 quantization which reduces compute requirements
questions.explanation: LLM decode is memory-bandwidth-bound: each token generation requires loading model weights from memory. Mobile DRAM at 50-90 GB/s versus datacenter HBM3 at 2-3 TB/s is a 30-50x bandwidth gap — the decisive bottleneck.

questions.question: What throughput does WebLLM achieve for Llama 3.1 8B Q4 on an M3 Max, and how does it compare to native inference?
options: ~10 tok/s, which is ~25% of native
~41 tok/s, which is roughly 70-80% of native
~80 tok/s, which matches native performance
~5 tok/s, which is ~10% of native due to WebGPU overhead
questions.explanation: WebLLM achieves ~41 tok/s for Llama 3.1 8B Q4 on M3 Max via WebGPU compute shaders — roughly 70-80% of native performance. This makes browser-based inference practical for smaller models.

questions.question: What is the recommended model format for iOS apps using the Apple Neural Engine in 2026?
options: GGUF Q4_K_M loaded via llama.cpp Metal backend
ONNX INT8 via the CoreML ONNX bridge
Core ML model with INT4 weights and FP16 activations
TensorRT-LLM FP8 compiled for A18 Neural Engine
questions.explanation: The lesson prescribes Core ML with INT4 weights and FP16 activations as the best practical path for iOS in 2026. The llama.cpp Metal backend uses MPS, not the ANE directly — native ANE requires Core ML conversion.

questions.question: The NVIDIA Jetson T4000 with JetPack 7.1 delivers approximately what performance relative to AGX Orin?
options: 0.5x AGX Orin
Same as AGX Orin
2x AGX Orin
5x AGX Orin
questions.explanation: The lesson states Jetson T4000 (JetPack 7.1) delivers 2x AGX Orin performance. The AGX Orin runs gpt-oss-20b via vLLM at ~40 tok/s, so T4000 targets ~80 tok/s on similar workloads.

questions.question: What is the 2026 mobile browser coverage for WebGPU, and which browser still had incomplete Android support?
options: ~40% coverage; Safari iOS was still missing
~70-75% coverage; Firefox Android was still catching up
~95% coverage; only older Android devices lacked support
100% on iOS; ~50% on Android with Chrome only
questions.explanation: WebGPU coverage in 2026 is approximately 70-75% of mobile devices. Chrome Android v121+ and Safari iOS 26 GA are supported; Firefox Android was still catching up.

questions.question: Which Qualcomm chip generation hits 45 TOPS in 2026 and what SDK enables LLM deployment on it?
options: Snapdragon 8 Gen 2; QNN SDK
Snapdragon X Elite / 8 Gen 4; QNN SDK and AI Hub
Snapdragon 8cx Gen 4; TensorRT Mobile
Snapdragon 7s Gen 3; ONNX Runtime
questions.explanation: Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite and 8 Gen 4 Hexagon DSPs hit 45 TOPS. The QNN (Qualcomm Neural Network) SDK and AI Hub provide conversion from PyTorch/ONNX, with Llama 3.2 and Phi-3 as first-class artifacts.
